CSRFTokenHeaderParameter.name: X-CSRF-Token
CSRFTokenHeaderParameter.description: Provides a CSRF token that was received earlier (required for all modifying operations). Note that such tokens eventually expire, so it is best to always send the most recently received token. It is not necessary, however, to fetch a specific CSRF token for certain operations: any previously received token will be acceptable, as long as it was received from the same server and has not yet expired.

Note that this normally corresponds to the key size, but can differ from it in case the standards have established a different number for indicating the strength, because the key sizes might have become too unfamiliar (such as for the PQC ML-DSA and SLH-DSA variants).

ca.description: Whether this is a CA certificate.

primarySAN.description: The primary (i.e. first) subject alternative name (SAN) of this certificate.

furtherSANs.description: The list of further subject alternative name (SAN) of this certificate. Note that the standard doesn't forbid duplicate SANs.

serial.description: The (decimal) serial number of this certificate.

fingerprint.description: The SHA-256 fingerprint of this certificate.

fingerprintMD5.description: The (legacy) MD5 fingerprint of this certificate.

fingerprintSHA1.description: The (legacy) SHA-1 fingerprint of this certificate.

hasStdKeyID.description: Whether this certificate contains a SubjectKeyIdentifier extension containing the standardized KeyID.

extKeyID.description: The KeyID which is declared in the SubjectKeyIdentifier extension of this certificate. Missing if no corresponding extension is present.

stdKeyID.description: The standardized KeyID calculated as the SHA-1 hash over the public key info of this certificate.

issued.description: The moment in time when this certificate was issued.

start.description: The moment in time when this certificate becomes valid.

end.description: The moment in time when this certificate expires.

validity.description: The duration for which this certificate is valid.

remainingDays.description: The integral number of remaining full 24h days for which this certificate is still valid. Note that when this field reports zero days, the certificate might still be valid for a couple of hours, i.e. the returned number of days are _at least_ that many full days of 24 hours.

revoked.description: The moment in time when this certificate was revoked.

trusted.description: The moment in time up to when this certificate is/was trusted.

message.description: The status message to describe the reason for rejection.

proto.description: The enrollment protocol that shall be recorded for this certificate.

session.description: The enrollment session ID. When given, must refer to an existing enrollment session for validation.

commonName.description: The common name (CN) for the certificate.

mail.description: The DN e-mail address for the certificate.

dnSuffix.description: The DN suffix for the certificate.

SID.description: The object SID for the user from Active Directory in its string form.

validityStart.description: The desired validity start. Might get adjusted to what is specified in the template to honor its limits.

validity.description: The desired validity duration. Might get adjusted to what is specified in the template to honor its limits.

returnIssuer.description: Whether to return the direct issuer CA certificate

returnChain.description: Whether to return any additional intermediate CA certificates, different from the direct issuer CA and the root CA

returnRoot.description: Whether to return the root CA certificate. Note that if the issuer is a root CA, it will be necessary to return the issuer certificate instead.

format.description: The desired format of returned data.

notify.description: The e-mail address of someone to notify upon completion.

renew.description: The old certificate to be renewed

CertificateRequestGen.description: Data for requesting a certificate without a CSR.

kind.description: The kind of key to generate.

ecCurve.description: The desired elliptic curve name for EC keys. May only be specified for EC keys.

size.description: The size of the key to generate. When given in combination with the EC curve name or a PQC kind with fixed key size, both must match.

CertificateRequestSign.description: Data for requesting a certificate with a CSR.

csr.description: The PKCS#10 certificate signing request (CSR). The JSON encoding requires this to be in Base64 form, so if PEM should be sent (i.e. with BEGIN/END header/footer lines), it will in effect be doubly Base64-encoded. Therefore it is recommended to directly pass the binary DER encoding in Base64-encoded form to JSON. If PEM is used, however, there is no explicit restriction on any line length of its Base64 encoded inner block between the BEGIN/END lines: any line length will be accepted, as long as it is on a separate line, distinct from the BEGIN/END delimiter lines (even a single long line is allowed).

cert.description: The requested certificate in the requested format.

issuer.description: The direct issuer CA certificate in the requested format. If this is a root CA certificate, it will _not_ be repeated in the 'root' field below.

chain.description: The chain of additional intermediate CA certificates, different from the direct issuer CA and the root CA, in the requested format.

endOfTrust.description: The instant in time up to when this certificate is considered trusted. When not given, the revocation time (when making this call) will be used, unless that is not within the certificate's validity period, in which case the start of that period will be used instead.

name.description: The name of this SAN. Syntax depends on the kind.
